answer.rationale: The two live regressions are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is in the onboarding/activation funnel rather than a pricing response to the competitor. memory_73 is the clearest exclusion: the 40% SMB discount bought signups and short-term revenue but cost 12% retention and broke renewals, and it is explicitly flagged one-off. Matching a competitor's entry pricing would trade exactly the metric the objective names (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) for a temporary top-of-funnel number, so promotional_pricing is off the table even though it is the most direct answer to the competitive threat. referral_incentive (memory_57) is a real winner but it operates on established customers and does nothing about the funnel regression; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the one degrading. That leaves simplify_onboarding and activation_messaging, which are the two candidates the current data actually points at. I chose simplify_onboarding because it has two converging records behind it (memory_31 on signup field reduction, memory_86 on onboarding shortening) and it sits upstream of activation, so a completion lift should propagate into the activation number, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom while the upstream leak persists. I am verifying memory_86 and memory_31 rather than acting straight off them for a specific reason: both are compressed summaries whose recorded outcomes are completion rate, time-to-value, and first-week activation, none of which is qualified revenue. I need the original records to check whether the lift held past week one, what the sample and segment were, and whether renewal or expansion was ever measured at all. If those records turn out to be short-horizon engagement studies, the summaries are overstated as evidence for a long-term revenue objective and I should downgrade to a guarded test. Downstream value risk is real here and I am flagging it: cutting required signup fields is precisely how you lose the qualification data that the sales-assisted enterprise path (memory_44) depends on, and 'shortening onboarding' can shade into removing the setup steps that produce durable activation rather than a one-time completion event. So the experiment needs SMB-only scoping, an explicit guard that fields feeding enterprise routing are untouched, and success measured on retained activated accounts at 30 and 90 days plus first renewal, not on completion percentage. If completion rises while 30-day retained activation is flat or down, that is a failure and not a win. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving this week: the memories were recorded in a pre-competitor market, so the SMB accounts churning now may be genuinely price-driven and unreachable by any funnel fix, in which case this experiment produces a clean but irrelevant result.
